new_entities.name: Night-shift work
new_entities.description: Occupational exposure to regular night-shift schedules, including fixed or rotating overnight work.

edges.effect_quant: Night-shift work shows a modest obesity signal in some pooled analyses, especially night-only schedules, but the overall literature is heterogeneous enough that the most defensible read is mixed rather than decisive harm.
edges.population: adult workers, especially nurses and other health professionals doing night shifts
edges.mechanism: Working against the circadian clock changes sleep timing, appetite hormones, meal timing, and opportunity for recovery, all of which plausibly nudge long-term weight gain upward. The biologic pathway is believable even though the epidemiology is noisier than the mechanism suggests.
edges.summary: The best current synthesis is not a slam dunk. A nurses-focused meta-analysis found a small obesity increase for night-only shift work, while an older health-professionals review was essentially null overall, so the right top-line conclusion is mixed evidence with a modest adverse drift in some subgroups.
edges.caveats: Different papers define shift work, obesity thresholds, and occupational groups very differently. That makes the subgroup signal more believable than any single pooled number.
